theory.intro: A **frequency distribution table** lists each score $x$ with its **frequency** $f$, the running total $cf$, and the proportion $rf$. From the table you can read the mode, median and mean.
facts: The **total frequency** $\Sigma f = n$ is the number of observations in the dataset.
The **cumulative frequency** $cf$ is the running total of the frequencies so far, and the last $cf$ equals $n$.
The **relative frequency** of a score is $rf = \dfrac{f}{n}$, and the relative frequencies always add to $1$.
The **mode** is the score $x$ with the largest frequency, not the frequency itself.
Find the **mean** from an $xf$ column: $\overline{x} = \dfrac{\Sigma xf}{\Sigma f}$.
The **median position** is $Mp = \dfrac{n + 1}{2}$, and the median is the first score whose $cf$ reaches $Mp$.
steps: List each distinct score $x$ in ascending order and tally the observations to determine each frequency $f$.
Calculate the cumulative frequency ($cf$) column by adding each frequency to the running sum.
Calculate the relative frequency column ($rf = \frac{f}{n}$) and the product column ($xf = x \times f$) as needed.
Sum the columns to find $\Sigma f$ and $\Sigma xf$, and compute summary statistics (mode, median position $Mp = \frac{n+1}{2}$, and mean $\overline{x} = \frac{\Sigma xf}{\Sigma f}$).

foundation.question_text:
Organise the following dataset into a frequency distribution table with scores ($x$) and frequencies ($f$):
$$3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5, 5, 6, 6, 7$$
State the total frequency $\Sigma f$.

Calculate the cumulative frequency ($cf$) for each score in the table:
$\begin{array}{c|c} x & f \\ \hline 1 & 4 \\ 2 & 7 \\ 3 & 6 \\ 4 & 2 \\ 5 & 1 \end{array}$
State the total number of observations $n$.

The frequency table shows the number of pets owned by $25$ households.
$\begin{array}{c|c} \text{Pets }(x) & \text{Frequency }(f) \\ \hline 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 14 \\ 2 & 5 \\ 3 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 \end{array}$
Identify the mode of the dataset.
foundation.solution_text:
The highest frequency is $14$, which corresponds to the score $x = 1$.
$\text{Mode} = 1\text{ pet}$

foundation.question_text:
Find the median score from the frequency table:
$\begin{array}{c|c|c} x & f & cf \\ \hline 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & 7 \\ 2 & 6 & 13 \\ 3 & 3 & 16 \\ 4 & 1 & 17 \end{array}$
foundation.solution_text:
$n = 17$
$Mp = \frac{17 + 1}{2} = 9$
The cumulative frequency first reaches or exceeds $9$ at $x = 2$ (where $cf = 13$).
$\text{Median} = 2$

foundation.question_text:
The table shows the number of goals scored by a team in $15$ matches.
$\begin{array}{c|c} x & f \\ \hline 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 4 \\ 3 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 \end{array}$
Complete the $xf$ column and calculate the mean number of goals $\overline{x}$.

The table shows the quiz scores out of $5$ for a group of students.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c} x & f & cf \\ \hline 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 \\ 3 & 8 & 14 \\ 4 & 5 & 19 \\ 5 & 3 & 22 \end{array}$
(i) How many students scored $3$ or less?
(ii) How many students scored more than $3$?
foundation.solution_text:
From the cumulative frequency column at $x = 3$:
(i) $14\text{ students scored } 3 \text{ or less}$
(ii) Students scoring more than $3$:
$22 - 14 = 8\text{ students}$

foundation.question_text:
A survey of $30$ people recorded the number of coffee cups consumed per day. The table has one missing frequency $k$.
$\begin{array}{c|c} \text{Cups }(x) & \text{Frequency }(f) \\ \hline 1 & 6 \\ 2 & 11 \\ 3 & k \\ 4 & 4 \end{array}$
Find the value of $k$, and calculate the relative frequency of drinking $2$ cups per day.
foundation.solution_text:
$\Sigma f = 30$
$6 + 11 + k + 4 = 30$
$21 + k = 30$
$k = 9$
$\text{Relative frequency for } x = 2 \text{ is } \frac{11}{30} \approx 0.367$

development.question_text:
The table shows the number of siblings of $40$ students. Complete the relative frequency ($rf$) and cumulative frequency ($cf$) columns.
$\begin{array}{c|c} x & f \\ \hline 0 & 5 \\ 1 & 18 \\ 2 & 12 \\ 3 & 4 \\ 4 & 1 \end{array}$

The scores in a mathematics test are tabulated below for $31$ students.
$\begin{array}{c|c} \text{Score }(x) & \text{Frequency }(f) \\ \hline 14 & 3 \\ 15 & 6 \\ 16 & 11 \\ 17 & 7 \\ 18 & 4 \end{array}$
Construct the cumulative frequency column and find the median score.

Calculate the exact mean of the following discrete distribution:
$\begin{array}{c|c} x & f \\ \hline 10 & 4 \\ 11 & 7 \\ 12 & 12 \\ 13 & 5 \\ 14 & 2 \end{array}$

A company records the number of overtime hours worked by $50$ employees in a week.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{Hours }(x) & \text{Frequency }(f) & cf \\ \hline 0 & 8 & 8 \\ 2 & 14 & 22 \\ 4 & 16 & 38 \\ 6 & 9 & 47 \\ 8 & 3 & 50 \end{array}$
What percentage of employees worked at least $4$ hours of overtime?
development.solution_text:
Employees working fewer than $4$ hours ($x \le 2$) is given by $cf$ at $x = 2$, which is $22$.
Employees working at least $4$ hours ($x \ge 4$):
$50 - 22 = 28$
$\text{Percentage} = \frac{28}{50} \times 100\%$
$= 56\%$

development.question_text:
A dataset has the following frequency distribution:
$\begin{array}{c|c} x & f \\ \hline 20 & 6 \\ 21 & 15 \\ 22 & 8 \\ 23 & 15 \\ 24 & 4 \end{array}$
State the mode(s) and explain whether the distribution is unimodal or bimodal.
development.solution_text:
The maximum frequency is $15$, which occurs at two distinct scores: $x = 21$ and $x = 23$.
$\text{Modes} = 21 \text{ and } 23$
The distribution is bimodal.

development.question_text:
A cumulative frequency table is given below. Reconstruct the individual frequencies $f$ for each score.
$\begin{array}{c|c} x & cf \\ \hline 5 & 4 \\ 6 & 10 \\ 7 & 23 \\ 8 & 31 \\ 9 & 35 \end{array}$

The table shows the number of books read by $28$ students over the holidays.
$\begin{array}{c|c} x & f \\ \hline 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 8 \\ 3 & 10 \\ 4 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 \end{array}$
Find the median position $Mp$ and determine the median.
development.solution_text:
$n = 28$
$Mp = \frac{28 + 1}{2} = 14.5$
Cumulative frequencies: $3, 11, 21, 26, 28$.
The 14th and 15th ordered values both fall in the group $x = 3$ (since $cf$ rises from $11$ to $21$).
$\text{Median} = 3$

mastery.question_text:
The frequency distribution below has an unknown frequency $k$. The mean of the dataset is known to be $\overline{x} = 2.4$.
$\begin{array}{c|c} x & f \\ \hline 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 8 \\ 3 & k \\ 4 & 3 \end{array}$
Find the value of $k$.

A dataset of $50$ observations has the following symmetric distribution with unknown frequencies $a$ and $b$:
$\begin{array}{c|c} x & f \\ \hline 1 & 4 \\ 2 & a \\ 3 & b \\ 4 & a \\ 5 & 4 \end{array}$
If the relative frequency of score $3$ is $0.36$, find the values of $a$ and $b$, and state the median.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Relative frequency of } 3 = \frac{b}{50} = 0.36 \implies b = 18$.
Total frequency: $4 + a + 18 + a + 4 = 50$
$26 + 2a = 50$
$2a = 24$
$a = 12$
$cf = [4, 16, 34, 46, 50]$
$Mp = \frac{50 + 1}{2} = 25.5$
$cf$ exceeds $25.5$ at $x = 3$.
$\text{Median} = 3$

mastery.question_text: A grouped frequency distribution has class intervals $10-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49$ with frequencies $8, 14, 12, 6$. Construct the relative frequency ($rf$) and cumulative frequency ($cf$) columns, and identify the modal class.
mastery.solution_text:
$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} \text{Class} & f & rf & cf \\ \hline 10-19 & 8 & 0.20 & 8 \\ 20-29 & 14 & 0.35 & 22 \\ 30-39 & 12 & 0.30 & 34 \\ 40-49 & 6 & 0.15 & 40 \end{array}$
$\Sigma f = 40$
$\Sigma rf = 1.00$
The highest frequency is $14$, which corresponds to the class $20-29$.
$\text{Modal class} = 20-29$
